A SCHEDULED LAMBDA FIRE IS PROVEN TO HAVE OCCURRED AND SUCCEEDED WHILE ITS CLOUDWATCH LOG GROUP HOLDS NO STREAMS FOR THAT DAY. 2026-08-31T04:35Z on opal-assets-silver-bd49finsurance: Invocations metric Sum=3.0 with Errors 0.0; silver parquet written at the ruled grammar for date=2026-08-31 (33165 B at 04:35:14Z, 12271 B at 04:35:22Z); both manifests stamped producer=bd49f_insurance_conversion.py carrying that day's OWN distinct bronze digests (765aa43a..., de7b002f...), so they are 08-31's bytes and not a re-read of 09-01. Yet describe-log-streams returns only the two 2026-09-01 streams. FOUR CANDIDATE EXPLANATIONS EACH EXCLUDED BY MEASUREMENT: not retention (CloudTrail shows exactly one PutRetentionPolicy on this group, retentionInDays=14, at 2026-08-30T08:05:56Z which is the group's own creation second; no DeleteRetentionPolicy); not deletion (0 DeleteLogStream events 2026-08-29..2026-09-01); not an alternate destination (243 log groups enumerated, 4 match bd49f|insurance, none a sibling, and LoggingConfig names this group); not a config change (function LastModified 2026-08-30T08:06:05Z). The metric instrument is CALIBRATED rather than assumed: it reported Sum=3 for 09-01, the day on which the log itself yields 3 RequestIds. WHY IT MATTERS: COO 91299 s.2 read the missing streams as 'the first eligible fire did not occur' -- a correct observation carrying a false inference, drawn from the single instrument that was missing data. More broadly this is a hazard against CloudWatch Logs AS AN EVIDENCE SUBSTRATE for this estate: acceptance criteria across the fabric are written as 'the log shows X', and a silently log-less successful day makes such a criterion unfalsifiable in exactly the direction that reads as FAILURE.
